sn46.14:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rajagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrel Sanctuary.
sn46.14:1.2: Now on that occasion the Venerable Mahakassapa was dwelling in the Pipphali Cave—sick, afflicted, gravely ill.
sn46.14:1.3: Then, in the evening, the Blessed One emerged from seclusion and approached the Venerable Mahakassapa. He sat down in the appointed seat and said to the Venerable Mahakassapa:
sn46.14:2.1: “I hope you are bearing up, Kassapa, I hope you are getting better. I hope that your painful feelings are subsiding and not increasing, and that their subsiding, not their increase, is to be discerned.”
sn46.14:2.2: “Venerable sir, I am not bearing up, I am not getting better. Strong painful feelings are increasing in me, not subsiding, and their increase, not their subsiding, is to be discerned.”
sn46.14:3.1: “These seven factors of enlightenment, Kassapa, have been rightly expounded by me; when developed and cultivated, they lead to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.
sn46.14:3.3: The enlightenment factor of mindfulness has been rightly expounded by me; when developed and cultivated, it leads to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna…. The enlightenment factor of equanimity has been rightly expounded by me; when developed and cultivated, it leads to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.
sn46.14:3.4: These seven factors of enlightenment, Kassapa, have been rightly expounded by me; when developed and cultivated, they lead to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, to Nibbāna.”
sn46.14:3.5: “Surely, Blessed One, they are factors of enlightenment!
sn46.14:3.6: Surely, Fortunate One, they are factors of enlightenment!”
sn46.14:4.1: This is what the Blessed One said.
sn46.14:4.2: Elated, the Venerable Mahakassapa delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.
sn46.14:4.3: And the Venerable Mahakassapa recovered from that illness.
sn46.14:4.4: In such a way the Venerable Mahakassapa was cured of his illness.
